title: THE STAFF IN HIS HAND
paragraphs:
THE STAFF IN HIS HAND
Exodus 4:2
Moses had been holding that staff for forty years.

It was not a weapon.
It was not a royal scepter.
It was not something impressive.
It was simply the walking stick of a shepherd.

For four decades in the wilderness of Midian, Moses used that staff for ordinary things.
To guide sheep.
To steady his steps on rocky hills.
To fend off wild animals.
Nothing about it looked powerful.
But one day, in the middle of the desert, God asked Moses a question that would change everything:

“What is that in your hand?”
— Exodus 4:2
God already knew the answer.
But the question was not about information.
It was about revelation.
Because Moses saw a shepherd’s stick.
God saw an instrument of deliverance.
The story begins at the burning bush.

Moses had fled Egypt forty years earlier after killing an Egyptian.
The prince of Egypt had become a forgotten shepherd in the wilderness.
The dreams of influence and leadership were gone.
Or so Moses thought.
Then one ordinary day, while tending sheep near Mount Horeb, something extraordinary happened.
A bush was burning.
But it was not consumed.
When Moses stepped closer, God called his name from the fire.
And suddenly the shepherd who had spent forty quiet years in obscurity was standing in the presence of the living God.
God gave him a mission that sounded impossible:
“Go back to Egypt.”
Not as a refugee.
Not as a fugitive.
But as the one who would confront Pharaoh and lead Israel out of slavery.
Moses immediately began listing reasons why he could not do it.

“Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh?”
“What if they do not believe me?”
“What if they will not listen to me?”
Moses saw his limitations.
But God pointed to what Moses already had.
“What is that in your hand?”
“A staff,” Moses replied.
That was it.
No army.
No throne.
No wealth.
Just a staff.
And yet that simple staff would become one of the most powerful symbols in the entire Bible.
When Moses threw the staff on the ground, it became a serpent.
When he picked it up again, it turned back into wood.
God was showing Moses something important:

The power was never in the staff.
The power was in God.
But God chose to work through something Moses already possessed.
And from that moment on, the Bible begins referring to it differently.
It is no longer just Moses’ staff.
In Exodus 4:20, Scripture calls it:
“The staff of God.”
The same piece of wood Moses once used to guide sheep would now guide the destiny of a nation.
With that staff in his hand:
Moses stretched it over the Nile and the water turned to blood.
He lifted it and plagues struck Egypt.
He raised it over the Red Sea and the waters split apart, forming walls on both sides.
An entire nation walked through the sea on dry ground.
Later in the wilderness, Moses struck the rock with the staff and water poured out for millions of thirsty people.
Even in battle against Amalek, when Moses held up his staff, Israel prevailed.
Again and again, that staff appeared at the center of God's miracles.
But remember this:
The wood was ordinary.
The difference was obedience.
Many people think God only uses impressive people with impressive resources.
But the Bible tells a different story.
God often begins with what seems small.
A sling in David’s hand.
Five loaves and two fish in a boy’s basket.
A widow’s small jar of oil.
And a shepherd’s staff in the desert.
Because the Kingdom of God does not run on human strength.
It runs on surrender.
God asked Moses a simple question.
But in reality, it is a question God still asks today.
“What is that in your hand?”
What ability do you already have?
What experience has God given you?
What influence do you carry?
What opportunities are already within reach?
Many people wait for God to give them something extraordinary.
But often God starts with something they already hold.
The staff of Moses reminds us of a powerful truth:

God does not need impressive tools.
He needs surrendered ones.
When Moses placed that staff in God’s service, it became a symbol of divine authority.
A shepherd’s tool became a weapon against oppression.
A simple piece of wood became part of the story of redemption.
And Pharaoh, the most powerful ruler of that time, would tremble before the God who worked through a shepherd and his staff.
Maybe today you feel like what you have is too small.
Too ordinary.
Too insignificant.
But Moses’ story reminds us that God specializes in using ordinary things for extraordinary purposes.
The question is not how impressive the tool is.
The question is whether it is placed in God’s hands.
Because when the ordinary is surrendered to God…

Seas can open.
Empires can shake.
And destinies can change.

“What is that in your hand?”
— Exodus 4:2
Take a moment and think about it.
What has God already placed in your hand that He might want to use for something greater?
